html:
The Chitimacha are a Native American people of the Mississippi delta in Louisiana, around the Atchafalaya Basin and Grand Lake. They spoke Chitimacha, a language with no known relatives.

Before contact they were one of the larger peoples of the lower Mississippi, living in towns among the bayous by fishing, gathering and farming. Their neighbours were the Atakapa to the west and the Natchez upriver.

When the French founded Louisiana, they fought the Chitimacha from 1706 to 1718. Many captives were sold as slaves. The survivors made peace and kept a small piece of their homeland at Charenton, and they are the only tribe in Louisiana that still holds part of its original land. The tribe is known for its double-woven river cane baskets. The map also shows the same people under the spelling Chitimacha.
sum: The Chitimacha are a Native American people of the Mississippi delta in Louisiana, around the Atchafalaya Basin and Grand Lake. They spoke Chitimacha, a language with no known relatives.
